section.title: Spotting for Thomas
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Above all a eulogy: every speaker laments his loss, tells how they bonded with him and what they loved about him, and celebrates him. The brief asks for nine people on their feet in one room, each saying what there is to say about the dead man: a eulogy, not a two-voice dialogue. Spine is mixed: Thomas is an original character and not in the corpus, so no event or scene names him; sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in (the Pragia aftermath, the run-up to Omega-4, Tuchanka, Rannoch, the Citadel shore leave, Grissom, the final push) and the speaker's own record of those. Jack holds the first and last turns (~2,500 words each, long as asked), the other seven run 450-1,000 (Grunt, EDI, James short and blunt; Liara, Joker, Tali fullest). Nine sections is inside the form's 6-14 range. Each turn opens by picking up the one before: Jack's grief to Tali's engine room, Tali's hospital-and-hands to Joker's bad days, Joker's jokes to Liara's late nights, Liara's mother story to Grunt's blunt question, Grunt's kitchen guarding to James's training and banter, James's Hammer glimpse to Wrex, Wrex's speech to EDI's data, EDI's four-leaf-clover tally back to Jack. Alcohol and music run through the turns as the room's furniture (Thomas's disco, pop, rock, rap, metal, folk, gabber, electro, and black-metal playlists, ryncol, the taped-up recipes), not as a section of their own. Canon branch: genophage cured, Wrex leads the krogan, geth-quarian peace (Legion dead), Grunt alive, Thane dead; crew do not know what Shepard chose, and his death is unconfirmed. Thomas's unfinished poems for Jack are private to Jack; the French lines are his to be quoted sparingly and, per memory rules, never verbatim-perfect by anyone but Jack.

required_facts.fact: Days after the destruction of the Bahak system's Alpha Relay, the galaxy is in turmoil over Commander Shepard's alleged role in the deaths of over 300,000 batarians. The Citadel Council publicly denounces Shepard, Alliance Councilor Donnel Udina works to deflect blame away from the Systems Alliance, and the Batarian Hegemony demands that Shepard be handed over for retribution. Shepard, having surrendered to Alliance authority, is confined and awaiting trial on Earth while the Normandy SR-2 is impounded and stripped of its Cerberus upgrades. On Omega, Alliance marine Lieutenant James Vega is drinking and playing cards in a bar, watching a newscast about the uproar over Shepard. Frustrated, he tears the screen from the wall and offers the krogan bartender payment for the damage. The batarians he had been playing cards with brand him a "Shepard Lover" and attack him; Vega fights the whole group off, smashing one man with the torn-out screen and crashing through a window with another. Admiral David Anderson arrives on Omega with a squad of soldiers and tells Vega he is being brought in for additional training. In an aircar on final approach to the docked Normandy SR-2, Anderson presses Vega to move past "the incident on Fehl Prime" and become the soldier the Alliance expects him to be. Vega, still carrying guilt over that mission, demands to be thrown in the brig instead. Anderson reveals that Vega will in fact be guarding the brig, and that it holds one very specific prisoner: Commander Shepard. The assignment places Vega aboard the Normandy and in Shepard's orbit just before the Reapers strike Earth, explaining his presence as a squadmate at the start of Mass Effect 3. A single omniscient narration panel in the comic assumes Shepard personally destroyed the Bahak relay; players who did not complete the Arrival mission may instead be told Alliance marines were responsible.

Roughly six months after the destruction of the Bahak system's mass relay and Commander Shepard's voluntary return to Alliance custody, Shepard was relieved of command and detained at a Systems Alliance facility in Vancouver on Earth, guarded by Lieutenant James Vega. As Alliance deep-space outposts beyond Sol began going dark without warning, Admiral Steven Hackett prepared for an imminent attack and Admiral David Anderson travelled to Vancouver to escort Shepard before an Alliance defence committee. Shepard confirmed the committee's worst fear: the Reapers had returned and were coming for Earth. During the hearing contact was lost with Luna Base and reports arrived of an unknown alien force landing in Earth's cities - the Reapers had already arrived. A Reaper capital ship descended through the clouds over Vancouver and fired on the Alliance building, killing the defence committee and most of the staff. Shepard and Anderson survived and fought on foot through the ruined city during the mission Prologue: Earth, contacting the Virmire survivor (Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko) by radio and ordering them to reach the Normandy. Anderson armed Shepard with an M-3 Predator; the pair crossed rooftops and rubble under fire from Oculi, husks and Cannibals while Reapers destroyed Alliance fighters and warships overhead. Anderson told Shepard they had to reach the Citadel and secure the Council's help. Reaching a comm unit by a crashed gunship, they hailed the Normandy SR-2, which bombed the area clear and set down to evacuate. Anderson refused to board, choosing to stay on Earth and lead the human resistance; he handed Shepard back the Commander's dog tags and charged Shepard with rallying the galaxy's forces. As the Normandy lifted away over burning human fleets, Shepard watched a child who had earlier been glimpsed hiding board an evacuation shuttle; the Kodiak was then shot down by a Reaper Destroyer, killing the boy - an image that recurred in Shepard's nightmares for the rest of the war. Aboard ship, James Vega protested leaving Earth, but Admiral Hackett contacted Shepard and assigned the next objective, Priority: Mars.

In the climactic endgame of Mass Effect 3, as Reaper forces ravaged Earth and the Crucible—an ancient superweapon built by the Protheans—required activation at the Citadel, Commander Shepard and Admiral David Anderson led a massive galactic assault on London, England. The Reapers had constructed a towering conduit—a massive structure built from organic and metallic components—in the war-torn city. This conduit, built according to mass relay principles but modified by Reaper technology, served as a direct transport mechanism connecting the ground of Earth to the Citadel, which had been mysteriously repositioned above the planet. The conduit functioned unlike standard mass relays: it emitted a constant, brilliant beam of blue light into the sky, continuously transporting matter (primarily the dead and dismembered remains of slaughtered populations) directly from Earth's surface to the Citadel. The structure had no visible element zero core and, critically, allowed living organic matter to survive transit—arriving at ballistic but survivable speeds—rather than disintegrating as with conventional relays. The Reapers appeared to have multiple destination termini on the Citadel, as different individuals arrived at separate points on the station. The assault ran in two ground stages. First Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" with M-920 Cain rounds so the Hammer ground force could land; the team then regrouped at a Forward Operating Base where Shepard held final words with surviving allies before Anderson gave the battle plan. The second stage pushed through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles coordinated with EDI on the Normandy destroyed a Reaper Destroyer blocking the road to the conduit. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final charge. The galactic assault on the conduit was devastating. Allied forces from across the galaxy—humans, turians, asari, salarians, quarians, krogan, and others— launched a coordinated ground assault to penetrate the structure and secure access to the Citadel. However, Harbinger, the Reaper flagship and commander of the local Reaper forces, personally defended the conduit with overwhelming firepower, killing or maiming most of the allied assault force. The majority of the attacking soldiers were annihilated, their bodies adding to the biomass flowing through the conduit itself. Despite the horrific casualties, Commander Shepard and Admiral Anderson managed to fight their way through the structure and reached its heart. Anderson, wounded but resolute, helped push Shepard toward the conduit's exit point. Shepard survived the ascent through the conduit and materialized on the Citadel, while Anderson arrived at a slightly different point on the station. Upon reaching the Citadel, Shepard gained access to the Crucible's control mechanisms and the Catalyst—the artificial intelligence that had guided the Reaper cycle for countless eons. At this critical juncture, Shepard was confronted with a series of final choices that would determine the fate of the galaxy: to Destroy all synthetic life (eliminating the Reapers and the geth but also killing EDI), to Control the Reapers (uploading Shepard's consciousness to command them), to achieve Synthesis (merging organic and synthetic life), or to Refuse the Catalyst's offer (allowing the cycle to continue unchanged). The consequences of this choice—affecting the survival of the geth, EDI, the Reapers themselves, and organic civilization—would echo across the galaxy for generations.
Most of the galactic assault force on Earth is killed or maimed; the conduit's light beam carries thousands of casualties toward the Citadel.

Per the final choice (Destroy/Control/Synthesis/Refusal): - Destroy: All Reapers are destroyed along with the entire geth species and EDI; synthetic life is eradicated; the cycle of extinction theoretically ends. - Control: Shepard's consciousness is uploaded into and merges with the Reaper collective, giving Shepard godlike power but ultimately disembodying them; the Reapers are brought under Shepard's control. - Synthesis: Shepard's genetic code is merged with all organic and synthetic life in the galaxy, creating a new form of hybrid existence; the Reapers are transformed into custodians of this new synthesis. - Refusal: The Catalyst and Reapers are allowed to proceed with the cycle; the Crucible fails and the Reapers continue the harvest; galactic extinction continues indefinitely.
Shepard's ultimate fate is determined by the choice made and the Crucible's firing.

If Destroy or Control are chosen and sufficient War Assets are gathered, Shepard survives (though potentially as a Reaper in Control ending or as a hybrid in Synthesis); otherwise Shepard dies in the Crucible's activation.
Depending on the ending, Anderson either survives (on the Citadel) or dies from wounds sustained during the assault.
The galaxy's future is fundamentally altered: either the Reapers are destroyed (ending the cycle), controlled by Shepard, synthetically merged with organics, or allowed to continue their harvest.
If Destroy is chosen, the geth and EDI are killed along with the Reapers; if Control or Synthesis is chosen, they survive and are transformed.

Per the Extended Cut: epilogue scenes show Admiral Hackett ordering the fleets to evacuate Earth's orbit, the Normandy caught in the energy wave in transit and crash-landing on a garden world, the Charon Relay's core breaking up while the relay itself survives and the mass relay network is later repaired, and a Liara time-capsule message. A fourth outcome, Refusal (declining to activate the Crucible or shooting the Catalyst), dooms the current cycle to the Reaper harvest but leaves records that let a later cycle break the pattern, shown in an alternate Stargazer scene. Shepard's name is added to the Normandy memorial wall beside Anderson's unless a high-strength Destroy leaves Shepard's survival ambiguous.

scenes.title: Sparring with Vega in the Shuttle Bay

beats.text: Vega keeps to the shuttle bay, by a weapons bench, trading banter with his friend Steve Cortez between missions. The first time Shepard comes down, James is doing pull-ups on the overhead bars. His greeting scales to how long Shepard took to visit: soon after Garrus comes aboard he just takes Shepard's word about the turian because he can't tell them apart; if EDI has a body he asks whether Shepard is "shitting" him; if Shepard left it a long time he wonders aloud what the Commander is doing below decks with the "grunts," or asks whether they took a wrong turn at the elevator.
However the first meeting goes, they end up in a sparring match. If Shepard put the visit off for a long time, James promises to go easy, "just in case."

Mid-spar, James gives the short version of his life before the Normandy. His old CO, Captain Toni — a hard-assed son of a bitch but a good leader — was killed with most of James's squad while they were protecting a civilian colony, Fehl Prime, from a Collector attack.

With Toni dead, command fell to James. He had to choose between saving the colony or saving the intel his squad had recovered — intel that could be used to destroy the Collectors. He saved the intel and let the colony fall, then learned too late that Shepard had wiped out the Collectors without it. The colony died for nothing, and that is the guilt he carries into the war.

scenes.when: 2186, Priority: Earth, before the armoured assault on the conduit

beats.text: The evac shuttle off the first landing zone reunited Shepard with Admiral Anderson, who introduced Major Coats, the officer who had covered the extraction. Anderson said it had taken the Reapers to bring the galaxy together; a squadmate answered that Shepard was the true unifying force.

At the FOB, Coats told Shepard how inspiring the Commander would be to the troops, then left to rejoin his unit. Shepard walked the base holding final conversations with the surviving squad — as few as three or as many as seven, depending on who had lived through the trilogy and whether Javik had been recruited.

On a ramp Shepard found Primarch Victus and, if he lived, Garrus; past a husk turret gun, Liara, whose mood turned on how many husks had got through; then Javik and the krogan leader giving a rallying speech to the troops, with Kirrahe or another STG officer alongside if Shepard had sabotaged the genophage under Wrex.

In the last room Shepard found EDI, Tali, and Anderson conferring with Coats. Anderson laid out the battle plan — a frontal armoured assault on the conduit past a parked Reaper Destroyer — and Shepard made an inspiring or grimly determined speech and picked the final squad.

variants.text: If Wreav rather than Wrex led the krogan, he gave the rallying speech in Wrex's place, and no salarian STG officer stood beside him.
If the geth wiped out the quarians at Rannoch, a Geth Prime stood in the final room where Tali would be; if the quarians won but Tali had died in Mass Effect 2, Admiral Raan took that place instead.
If Garrus did not survive, only Victus stood on the ramp and the squad Shepard said goodbye to was smaller.

With Captain Toni down, Lieutenant James Vega takes command. In the counterattack Kamille and Essex flank the mercs — Kamille firing heavy, Essex covering with biotics — and cut through their ranks.

evidence.page: The Blood Pack Siege of Fehl Prime
evidence.text: The Blood Pack Siege of Fehl Prime. 2183, when Blood Pack mercenaries lay siege to the Fehl Prime colony the Fehl Prime colony When Archuk, the Blood Pack's krogan leader, challenges Delta Squad to show themselves, Vega duels him head-on to hold the mercs' attention while Kamille and Essex flank. Milque hands Vega his power cells and covers the duel with sniper fire, and Nicky's combat drone overloads Archuk's shields. Archuk grazes Milque across the collarbone and nearly beats Vega down, but Milque recovers and kills Archuk, saving Vega. The Blood Pack are defeated; the krogan Brood is spared and taken prisoner.

During the Collector attacks of 2185, James Vega and his squad were stationed on Fehl Prime. When the Collectors struck the colony, James was forced to choose between defending the colonists and retrieving intel about the Collectors that could potentially be used to destroy them. James goes for the intel while his squad stays behind, resulting in their deaths and the abduction of the rest of the colony. The Alliance later commends James for his actions, even though Commander Shepard ultimately ends the Collector threat and renders James' intel unnecessary.

Anderson along with Admiral Hackett commends Delta Squad for its heroic and selfless actions against the Blood Pack mercenaries on the colony of Fehl Prime. Anderson congratulates Lieutenant James Vega for his leadership role in a "hell of a battle" which is expected of combat veterans. In 2185, after the Collector attack on Fehl Prime has been defeated at the cost of almost all the colonists and much of the infrastructure, Anderson commends Lt. Vega yet again. Anderson asserts that Vega's actions have placed vital intel about the Collectors into Alliance possession which can not only gives them a tactical advantage over their opponents but also provides new weapons and ships research. After Hackett pins the medal of honor promoting Vega to Lt. Commander onto his uniform, Anderson gives Vega new orders. Seeing Vega's efforts to follow in Shepard's footsteps, Anderson tells him that he may have the oppurtunity to work with Shepard one day as rumors of their death are premature. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Milque was a human sniper and member of Delta Squad, an Alliance special-forces unit deployed to the colony of Fehl Prime, as depicted in the animated film Mass Effect: Paragon Lost. A cautious, cynical man with a dry sense of humor, he was often taken for a coward but obeyed orders and reliably covered his teammates, usually in exchange for free drinks. Armed with an M-92 Mantis, he was the squad's marksman.

Delta Squad first arrived on Fehl Prime around 2183 to repel a Blood Pack mercenary attack. Milque's unit was shot down during a strafing run from a Kodiak shuttle; Lieutenant James Vega took command after Captain Toni was incapacitated. Milque surrendered his power cells to Vega, covered his charge against the krogan Battlemaster Archuk, was grazed across the collarbone by the mercenary Brood, and recovered in time to kill Archuk and save Vega. The Blood Pack were defeated and Milque was commended.

Two years later, with Fehl Prime rebuilt and fortified with an anti-ship cannon, Delta Squad investigated a jamming signal and found an alien artifact, which Vega ordered destroyed. The colony was then attacked by the Collectors, who harvested colonists aboard a ship. The squad's counterattacks failed; the defense cannon could not penetrate the ship's barriers, and a Praetorian containing Kamille's torso killed Mason. The survivors escaped in the imprisoned Brood's ship in exchange for freeing him. Vega spiked the group's drink flask with a cure for the seeker plague. Brood was shot dead by the Cerberus informant Messner while attacking the Collector ship, and the group was captured. Milque, Essex and Vega synthesized more antidote through the Collectors' systems and revived the colonists. Milque, who had washed out of pilot training, was made to fly a captured freighter, using it to rescue Vega at the ship's core. Forced to choose, Vega saved Treeya and her intel rather than the colonists, and the Collector ship crashed with everyone aboard killed; Milque judged it the wrong choice. Vega was later commended, promoted and invited into the N7 program. Milque joined Vega and Treeya at the Fehl Prime Memorial Monument to honor the dead.

Meanwhile, the Collector ship starts descending into the planet's atmosphere as its drive core is disabled. However, the pod containing Treeya that was vented into space earlier starts descending into the atmosphere as well. After Vega hops aboard the freighter, he orders Milque to head for the now\-awakened colonists and pick up Treeya afterwards. Treeya counters that there's no time and that James only has enough to save one or the other. The asari obtained valuable intel about the Collectors earlier, further complicating Vega's thought processes. Milque is indecisive, deferring to whatever choice Vega makes, although frantically urging the Lieutenant to make up his mind before it's too late to save either. Flash forward to the Citadel, Vega just finished giving his report to Anderson and Admiral Hackett and is given a commendation and a promotion for his actions on Fehl Prime along with a set of new orders. Milque, curious, asks the big man what else he got, snatching Vega's orders from him, and learns that the Lieutenant Commander just got an invitation to the N7 program. Milque comments that now the big man is definitely in the league of Commander Shepard. Vega, who has been mentally scarred by the events, thanks Milque but says he doesn't deserve it. Milque is embarrassed at speaking out of turn and asserts that he is ready to follow Vega anywhere. Milque accompanies the Lieutenant Commander back to Fehl Prime, where Vega flashes back to the critical juncture in his life that led to his present state. Back aboard the freighter, Milque asks James what to do, with time running out fast and both Treeya and the colonists' lives in jeopardy. Vega snatches the controls from Milque, steering the ship towards Treeya's pod and the intel she got. Milque is horrified at seeing the Collector ship carrying all the colonists on board burn; everyone killed in a powerful explosion as the ship impacts the surface. At the time, he judged Vega has made the wrong choice. Milque later joins Vega and Treeya at the Memorial Monument on Fehl Prime dedicated to all of its lost souls, paying homage to the fallen. ##

Admiral Hackett along with Admiral Anderson commends Delta Squad for its exceptional performance against the Blood Pack mercenaries on Fehl Prime in 2183\. Lieutenant James Vega's actions during the mission strike Hackett as similar to those of Commander Shepard. Hackett also delivers additional orders to the Delta Squad to protect valuable Alliance interests on Fehl Prime. When Vega protests, Hackett reminds him of the chain of command and assures him that Delta Squad's mission will be of vital importance to the Alliance. Hackett also cautions Vega about the dangers associated with trying to follow in Shepard's footsteps which usually involve the burden of excessive death and destruction. After the Collector attack on the colony and the subsequent destruction of the Collector ship and the deaths of almost all the colonists, Hackett again commends Vega for his heroic and selfless actions, this time on the Citadel. He honors Vega with a medal for his actions and promotes him to Lieutenant Commander. Seeing Vega fighting so hard to be like Shepard, Hackett tells him that he may have the chance to work with the Commander one day as rumors of Shepard's death were premature. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

During the colonist abductions on Fehl Prime, the Collectors unleash a Praetorian to thwart the efforts of the locals disrupting their operations. This Praetorian was created in part from one of the Delta Squad marines, Kamille. As with the Praetorians encountered by Shepard, It can withstand constant firepower. However, its attacks are all of a green color compared to the standard blue, likewise with its barrier protection. This Praetorian was destroyed by James Vega, in great part thanks to Essex disabling its barrier.

A merchant named Messner volunteers his used Mako for transporting James Vega, his Delta Squad, and archaeologist Treeya Nuwani to Prothean ruins on Fehl Prime. James assigns the vehicle's driver Mason to watch their backs with the Mako's gun while the rest disembark to locate the source of interference jamming the colony's comm systems. Following the arrival of the Collectors, James and the group use the Mako to make haste toward the colony. While the rest plan on doing more recon on foot, the sniper Milque volunteers to stay and "guard" the Mako, prompting his teammate Kamille to disdain his seeming cowardice. However, subsequent events render the Mako irrelevant at best, or destroyed at worst, along with the entire colony. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

In 2183, the human colony of Fehl Prime, a major producer of pharmaceuticals for the Systems Alliance, comes under attack by a group of Blood Pack mercenaries led by the krogan Archuk. In response, the Alliance dispatches several teams of Marines to aid the beleaguered colonists. During the landing attempt, each of the Alliance shuttles are shot down by the Blood Pack. Only one Marine unit, Delta Squad, survives the crash landing of their shuttle, but the Blood Pack execute several members before the rest can retreat to cover. Lieutenant James Vega stays behind to help Delta Squad's commanding officer, Captain Toni, whose leg was badly broken in the crash. Vega sets Toni's leg, causing him to scream and alert the Blood Pack to their presence. Under heavy fire, Vega and Toni scramble to meet up with the rest of the squad, consisting of Kamille, Nicky, Milque, Essex, and Mason. When Archuk challenges Delta Squad to show themselves and fight, Vega decides to duel Archuk, distracting the Blood Pack while Kamille and Essex flank them and ambush from behind. Nicky aids Vega by sending out a combat drone, while Milque provides covering fire with his sniper rifle. At first, Vega is outmatched by Archuk, unable to penetrate the krogan's heavy shields, but with the help of Nicky's drone, Archuk's shields are overloaded and Vega is able to chip away at his armor. Archuk charges and grabs Vega, but Milque kills the krogan before Archuk can strike the final blow. Meanwhile, Kamille and Essex take out the remaining Blood Pack. The sole survivor, Archuk's second\-in\-command Brood, is spared by Vega and taken prisoner. In the aftermath, Admiral Steven Hackett orders Delta Squad to remain on Fehl Prime and protect it from future attacks.

Nicky was a member of Delta Squad, an Alliance special forces unit deployed to the colony of Fehl Prime in 2185, as depicted in the animated film Mass Effect: Paragon Lost. He served as the team's technical specialist and was highly talented at his job, though shy and timid. He respected the chain of command and showed great deference to Lieutenant James Vega, persistently calling him "sir" despite Vega's objections.

Delta Squad was sent to Fehl Prime to stop a Blood Pack invasion. Worried by the last-minute orders, Nicky analyzed the mission thoroughly. The Kodiak shuttle was shot down during descent. In the counter-assault Nicky provided tactical readouts of enemy positions and deployed his Combat Drone, which distracted the Blood Pack leader Archuk long enough to buy Vega time. Nicky was then wounded by a sniper shot from Brood and was incapacitated for the rest of the firefight. He was commended afterward.

Two years later, with Fehl Prime flourishing but new defense cannons installed amid a spate of Terminus colony disappearances, Nicky suspected the guns were connected to those disappearances. Captain Toni ordered Delta Squad to investigate a jamming signal emitted by an alien artifact in nearby Prothean ruins; the artifact was destroyed by Essex after Nicky failed to interface with it. When a Collector ship arrived, Nicky could not contact the colony. The squad tried to use the colony defense cannons against the vessel, but Vega, impatient with the slow charge, ordered a half-power shot that was deflected and nearly killed the team. Retreating into a bunker, Nicky's database search for an antidote to seeker-swarm toxin instead flagged squad member Messner as a Cerberus operative, forcing an uneasy alliance. After a Praetorian attack drove the squad onto Brood's ship, the creature attacked the shuttle in flight; Nicky was mortally wounded by its leg while pushing Vega clear of a melee attack. As he died, he urged Vega to save the colonists.

Messner was a trader who arrived on Fehl Prime in 2185, presenting himself as a traveling merchant selling hardware around the galaxy. In truth he was a Cerberus operative tasked with investigating the disappearances of human colonies and the Collectors' involvement, as depicted in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost.

Delivering a shipment to Fehl Prime, Messner met James Vega and Treeya en route to the colony's underground research labs, flattering Vega for his 2183 victory. Barred from the newly secured labs, he lent Delta Squad a M35 Mako to investigate a jamming signal on the colony outskirts. While the squad destroyed the alien bio-mechanical device producing the signal, a Collector ship arrived and began harvesting the population; Messner suggested using the colony defense cannons against it, but a low-powered shot failed to disable the ship. In the labs Delta Squad learned the tightened security had been meant to keep Messner out, the Alliance having identified him as a Cerberus agent. He admitted it, arguing they now shared the goal of stopping the Collectors.

When Delta Squad used a ship piloted by the krogan Brood to attack the Collector ship's drive core, Messner shot Brood in the head, causing the ship to crash and the squad to be captured. He revealed he had deliberately lured the Collectors to Fehl Prime with the jamming device to study them, sacrificing the colony to gain their temporary trust. He forced Treeya, who could interface with Prothean technology, to access a Prothean archive aboard the ship, revealing the Protheans' last stand, their transformation into Collectors, and a plan to liquefy humans into genetic material for a new Reaper. Messner recorded the intel on a bracelet for Cerberus. The Collectors then declared him no longer useful and prepared a pod for his "ascension"; he threw Treeya into it instead, but she seized the bracelet as the pod was ejected toward Fehl Prime. In the ensuing firefight Vega disarmed and stabbed Messner, refused his bribes, and left him to be killed by Collector fire.

Lieutenant James Vega was a human Systems Alliance Marine and a member of Commander Shepard's squad in 2186. An experienced soldier but unfamiliar with galactic politics and the criminal underworld, he was written primarily by Mac Walters and intended to reflect a new player's perspective. He was originally named James Sanders before the name was changed.

Per Mass Effect: Homeworlds, Vega joined the Marines at Camp Pendleton in 2176 with the encouragement of his uncle Emilio Vega, despite his father Joshua "Josh" Sanders trying to trap him into a life as an errand boy through a coerced drug run in San Diego. Emilio convinced James that only he could choose how to live.

In Mass Effect: Paragon Lost, Vega served as second-in-command of Delta Squad on the colony Fehl Prime under Captain Toni. After defeating a Blood Pack siege in single combat with the krogan Archuk, Delta Squad was assigned as colony security. Two years later the Collectors attacked; with Toni incapacitated, Vega took command. His decision to fire the colony defense cannons at half power failed, alerting the Collector ship. Betrayed by the undercover Cerberus/Collector agent Messner, and unable to save both the asari anthropologist Treeya (who carried vital intel) and the colonists, Vega chose to save Treeya and the intel, sacrificing the colony. He was commended and promoted but felt he was no hero. He later learned Shepard had destroyed the Collectors without the intel, meaning the colony died for nothing. This guilt drove him to reckless behavior. In Mass Effect: Conviction, Anderson recruited him from Omega to guard the Alliance brig holding the surrendered Shepard.

In Mass Effect 3, Vega escorted Shepard to the defense committee hearing interrupted by the Reaper attack on Earth, then helped extract Shepard aboard the Normandy. On Mars he crashed his shuttle into Dr. Eva Coré's to stop her escaping with the Prothean data. He served as squadmate throughout the war, based in the Shuttle Bay bantering with his friend Steve Cortez, doing pull-ups, and sparring with Shepard, to whom he confided the Fehl Prime story. He nicknamed people ("Loco" for male Shepard, "Lola" for female, "Scars" for Garrus, "Sparks" for Tali, "Esteban" for Cortez). He noted his father's surname was Sanders but that he was unrelated to Kahlee Sanders. Offered N7 training and doubtful he deserved it, he ultimately accepted, celebrating with a back tattoo. A female Shepard with no prior commitments could romance him. If Shepard could not rally enough forces, Vega could be killed by Harbinger during the final push to the conduit; otherwise he survived and honored Shepard at the Memorial Wall. He was voiced by Freddie Prinze, Jr.

evidence.text: - One Mass Effect 3 Online Pass. - Four weapons: - N7 Hurricane Submachine Gun - N7 Crusader Shotgun - N7 Valiant Sniper Rifle - N7 Eagle Heavy Pistol - One alternate squadmate outfit each for: - Ashley Williams - Kaidan Alenko - James Vega - Liara T'Soni - One casual outfit for Commander Shepard (N7 Hoodie). - KEI\-9, a robotic dog that patrols the Shuttle Bay of the Normandy SR\-2.

*For his gameplay attributes, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 3\)\#James Vega.* James Vega is tasked to escort Shepard to an Alliance defense committee hearing, but the hearing is interrupted when the Reapers attack Earth. Vega and Ashley Williams/Kaidan Alenko (depending on who survived Virmire) retrieve the Normandy SR\-2 and extract Shepard. Voluntarily staying behind to help organize a resistance, Anderson convinces Shepard to leave Earth to seek help from the Citadel Council. Vega is displeased on hearing this and wants to stay behind as well; Shepard overrules him with the stark military logic of the plan, upsetting Vega who nonetheless lets the matter drop for now. During a mission to the Prothean archives on Mars, after Shepard and Ashley/Kaidan reunite with Liara, Shepard sends Vega outside the research facility to safeguard the team's exit. While this order again frustrates James, it proves very fortuitous. Dr. Eva Coré, revealed to be a Cerberus mole, almost escapes Mars in possession of the only remaining copy of translated Prothean data that may contain the secret to defeating the Reapers, but a waiting Vega crashes his own shuttle into hers, narrowly averting disaster. Eva, further revealed to be a synthetic in the crash, is disabled by Shepard, and the Commander orders the squad to her back with them. Vega complies, slinging the seemingly lifeless android over his shoulder and dumping it in the medbay outside the AI Core. Later on the Citadel, Shepard may speak with Vega again on the Presidium under relaxed circumstances for the first time since Vancouver. Vega comments on the quiet, noting how peaceful the Citadel is, pointing out its only a facade because the people living there are isolated from the Reaper threat and are in denial. Vega finally admits that leaving Earth was the correct decision for Shepard to make; the other races needed the wake\-up call, and humanity can't stop the Reapers without their help. As the Commander is leaving, James says he's heading down to the parts of the Citadel where they "keep it real" if Shepard wants to meet him there sometime. Vega normally loiters in the Shuttle Bay by a weapons bench, occasionally bantering with his good friend Steve Cortez over topics of interest. The first time Shepard visits Vega in the Shuttle Bay, James is doing some pull\-ups using the overhead bars in his turf. Depending on how far along Shepard is on the track to saving the galaxy, Vega's reactions run the whole gamut. Immediately after Shepard debriefs the Council about the Crucible, getting the usual noncommittal and unhelpful responses and being informed they have to rescue a turian primarch from Palaven, James reveals he's never been to the turian homeworld. If he was doing pull\-ups by the time Garrus is welcomed aboard, he says he'll take Shepard's word about the turian for it as he can't tell turians apart. If EDI's got herself a shiny robot body, Vega asks instead if Shepard was "shitting" him, and his Commander replies "I shit you not." If Shepard is male, James poses the question if he's just there to inform him about EDI. If Shepard delays talking to him for much farther, James wonders instead what the Commander is doing below decks with the "grunts", voicing aloud he was starting to think Shepard doesn't like him. If Shepard really delayed in talking to him, the first thing Vega asks the Commander is if they "took a wrong turn at the elevator", by now firmly thinking Shepard didn't know or cared to know where to find him. Whatever the circumstances of their first meet, they eventually get into a sparring match, where James gives a brief summary of his activities before joining the Normandy. If Shepard really refrained from talking to him James promises to go easy, "just in case." James narrates that his old CO, Captain Toni, a "hard\-assed son of a bitch" but a "good leader" in Vega's words, was killed along with most of Vega's squad while the squad was protecting a civilian colony from a Collector attack. The leadership vacuum caused by Captain Toni falling in battle was filled in by Vega himself, and he had to make a choice between saving the colony or saving the intel the squad had recovered that could be used to destroy the Collectors. Vega chose to save the intel, but found out far too late that his choice was rendered completely unnecessary since Shepard managed to destroy the Collector threat without the intel Vega saved, which meant that Vega allowed the colony to die for nothing.

However, Kamille is abducted by the Collectors in the chaos. Outside the bunker's entrance, Vega and Essex hold off hordes of enemies while Nicky hacks through the bunker security. Mason and Milque then arrive in the nick of time and seal off the Collectors' approach by causing a cave\-in. Mason is furious at Essex for failing to watch Kamille's back. Vega chastises them for quarreling and shouts at them to fall back. The squad retreats into the bunker with Essex covering them with his biotics. Once inside, Vega formulates a new plan: to escape in the freighter Messner arrived in. However, the plan doesn't last long as the Collector vessel incinerates the ship as if it has heard Vega's plan. Messner then brings up Vega's unintended wrong choice, which causes Mason to vent his fury at him. Vega unflinchingly says that he hasn't given up on anyone yet and stresses the necessity of fighting together and setting aside differences. He and Nicky then proceed to bring Essex's paralyzed form inside the bunker. Vega orders Nicky to use the Alliance databases to find a possible cure for the paralysis. While searching, Nicky comes up with a startling find: Messner is an undercover Cerberus agent. Vega is furious at this revelation, hitting Messner across the face while explaining to Treeya about Cerberus goals. He relents once Messner asserts Cerberus is looking for a cure to the seeker swarm paralysis too. A new distraction occurs when Brood, who is being kept as a test subject in the labs, struggles to free himself from confinement. Vega quickly goes to meet Brood and despite Brood's promises to help them escape the colony, decides not to trust him. Later, being by himself while Nicky continues the search for a cure, Vega reflects on his past decisions. Noticing how he is awfully quiet, Treeya comes to console Vega. Vega quietly asks if he made the right decision to fire the defense cannons at half power. Treeya honestly answers that he made what he thought was the best choice. When Vega talks about how Shepard would have made the right choice, Treeya firmly tells him Vega is not Shepard and that he should stop trying to act like him/her. She then bonds briefly with Vega who experiences a moment of peace. Nicky finally finds a cure which however fails to show any immediate effect on Essex. A Praetorian suddenly attacks the lab and tears through it, claiming the life of Mason, who impulsively approaches it on seeing Kamille's twisted form inside the creature's head. Vega and Milque open heavy fire on the Praetorian, but are unable to penetrate the heavy armor. While falling back, Vega decides to take a quick detour and frees Brood after forming an uneasy alliance. Brood leads the way to a hidden shuttle of his and the team board it and tries to get away as fast as it can. The Praetorian follows however and despite the sustained fire from Vega, Milque and Nicky, it manages to stab the latter in the gut when he steps in to take the blow meant for Vega, wounding him mortally. Vega, aghast and furious at the casualty, jumps onto the Praetorian's back which is now held in a stasis by a revived Essex. Vega discharges his gun into the Praetorian's skull at point\-blank range and the enemy is defeated at last, falling into the industrial vats. After being hauled back into the ship by Essex, Vega immediately goes to a dying Nicky and tries to apply first\-aid but his efforts are in vain as the marine breathes his last after urging Vega to save the colonists. Hidden for the moment, the squad sets the shuttle down in a safe spot and commences repairs. Vega decides to take the fight to the Collectors by infiltrating their ship. Quietly, he slips the seeker swarm antidote into his flask containing a drink and offers it to everyone, encouraging them to use Brood's idea of punching straight through the Collector weapons port. The plan is then to disable the ship's drive core and save the colonists. The shuttle then goes airborne and punches through the desired spot flawlessly. Vega, Essex and Milque then proceed to defend the shuttle from incoming Collector troopers, using Brood's store of heavy weapons. Even Treeya joins the fight and Vega compliments her, causing her to blush. Messner shows his true colors at this time and shoots Brood in the head as he is about to take out the drive core, causing the shuttle to make a crash landing. Vega, Essex and Milque are captured and paralyzed by the Collectors while Treeya is forced away by Messner, who is actually working for the Collectors.

Priority: Mars was the first full mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically after the Reaper assault on Earth in the prologue. Admiral Hackett ordered the Normandy to the Prothean archives on Mars, where the dig site had gone silent, to recover data that might help defeat the Reapers. Shepard landed with James Vega and found Cerberus troops executing Alliance researchers; this was the first appearance of Cerberus as an enemy faction in the trilogy, introducing Assault Troopers, Centurions and Guardians. Among the dead was a researcher named Reeves.

Inside the facility Shepard reunited with Dr. Liara T'Soni, who revealed she had discovered Prothean plans for a device ("the Crucible") capable of stopping the Reapers, and that Cerberus was there to seize them. Shepard sent Vega back to the shuttle to protect the team's exit and took Liara as squadmate. The two fought through the research complex, a sabotaged cafeteria where the air had been vented, corridors, a clean room, an autoturret gauntlet and a tram station, learning that Cerberus operatives had been implanted with Reaper technology. Shepard posed as a Cerberus team to lure a tram, then fought through a large battle at the archive station.

In the archive chamber the Illusive Man appeared by hologram. The Cerberus infiltrator Dr. Eva Coré was caught stealing the Prothean data, triggering a rooftop chase. Eva reached a shuttle, but Vega crashed his shuttle into hers. Her organic disguise was destroyed, revealing a mech infiltration unit, and on the Illusive Man's order she gravely injured Kaidan Alenko or Ashley Williams before Shepard shot her down. Shepard ordered the body brought aboard the Normandy, which left Mars orbit just as the Reapers arrived. The wounded crewmate was taken to the medical bay, and Shepard ordered Joker to set course for the Citadel. Hackett confirmed Anderson's order to seek Council aid and requested the Crucible plans for Alliance analysis. Eva's body would later be reactivated by EDI.

evidence.page: Mass Effect 3: N7 Collector's Edition Pack
evidence.text: The Mass Effect 3: N7 Collector's Edition Pack was a DLC pack exclusive to buyers of the Mass Effect 3 N7 Collector's Edition, the N7 Digital Deluxe Edition, or the Mass Effect 3 DLC Bundle on Origin, and later included in Mass Effect Legendary Edition. Its contents were one Mass Effect 3 Online Pass; four N7-styled weapons (the N7 Hurricane submachine gun, N7 Crusader shotgun, N7 Valiant sniper rifle, and N7 Eagle heavy pistol); one alternate squadmate outfit each for Ashley Williams, Kaidan Alenko, James Vega and Liara T'Soni; a casual N7 Hoodie outfit for Commander Shepard; and KEI-9, a robotic dog that patrols the Shuttle Bay of the Normandy SR-2. The N7 Valkyrie assault rifle shares the same N7 aesthetic as the four included weapons.

- As the squad takes in the spectacle of the Reaper towering over them, Ashley will comment "Demons do exist and they want to kill us all." - After Liara recommends following the Reaper in order to escape the killzone, Ashley will comment on the absurdity of such a notion. - When Liara and Shepard discuss finally ending the "nightmare" of the Reapers, Ashley vehemently agrees, saying it feels like they've been fighting the Reapers "forever." - When husks attack on final approach to the temple, Ashley warns, "Shit! We've got husks incoming!" - When Harvesters show up, Ashley exclaims, "Damn! A flying wall of death just showed up!" - As the asari gunship pilots provide fire support, Ashley will exclaim "That's the best damn asari pilot!" - While fighting Kai Leng, Ashley will angrily ask Shepard for permission to tear the assassin's head off, when taunting the Commander over Thane Krios'/Major Kirrahe's death. - During Priority: Horizon: - Upon being confronted by Phantoms near the start of the level, Ashley will snarl, "I hate these guys!" - Upon emptying the pool of water, Ashley will notice the Reaper tech, stating that she'd recognize it anywhere. - During Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy: - At the very start, when CAT6 mercs arrive, Ashley shouts, "Let's kill these guys." - If James complains about his training weights being messed around during the elevator ride down the shuttle bay, Ashley will start to ask James about his weight training goals, but will then think better of it. - Priority: Cerberus Headquarters: - After the squad has breached the Hangar doors and defeated the Cerberus counterattack, Ashley remarks, "Let's get moving then. I'm sick of this place already." - If Ashley is brought as a squadmate she will express horror upon learning that Cerberus is throwing troops at the squad, whom are simply indoctrinated civilians. - When the Alliance Fleet opens fire on the station, Ashley comments, "Fifth Fleet's hitting 'em hard." - When the first Phantom appears, Ashley will say, "Here come the girls!" After the Phantom is defeated, Ashley will say, "Try jumping now!" - While moving past the remains of the Proto\-Reaper, Ashley will whisper "That thing's freaking me out, like it's watching us". Shepard will reply that "\[i]t tried to kill me last time, it can watch all it wants".

Shepard can invite Vega and Cortez for a night of drinks and watching biotiball featuring the Seattle Sorcerers taking on the Usaru Maestros, before or after the party. Cortez sends an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. Both Cortez and Vega state their cases for each team to win. Vega backs the Maestros and is teased by Cortez for it, who cites Vega's support of the Maestros is mostly due to their players being beautiful asari, than their actual skill. Vega sheepishly admits he has got the "hots" for the Maestro players. Shepard is asked to back a team. Selecting a particular team will result in the supporter of that team winning the bet (though the Sorcerers always win the game). Vega is disappointed when his team doesn't win and grudgingly admits defeat. When Shepard questions the nature of the bet, the winner reveals that the bet was only on whether the Commander would be correct in their pick, rather than who would actually win. After the game, both of them thank Shepard and leave the apartment. Vega is a mandatory invite to Shepard's big party. During the party a female Shepard with no prior commitments can support a hook\-up between herself and James. If this happens Shepard will wake up the next morning with James; however, he asks Shepard to not mention what happened to anyone else. In the first stages of the party Vega hangs out with Cortez on the couches in the living room. If Shepard sets a quiet party, James hangs out with Liara by the bar at the poker den, engaging in a debate over which ship is better: the SSV Normandy or the Normandy SR\-2. James favors the latter. At the conclusion of a quiet party, Vega plays poker with Liara in the den. If the party is set to energetic, James spends time at the apartment balcony with Liara and some of the other biotics in the party, namely Liara, Jacob, Jack, Miranda, and Kaidan/Ashley, if they're present. Vega claims physical training trumps biotics, much to the incredulity of the others. Liara challenges this claim and both of them exchange friendly barbs, with the others supporting Liara. Vega then proceeds to show off his "fine example of peak physical form". Ashley, if present, shows interest beyond professionalism in Vega, to which he reacts favorably. If Shepard favors physical training, James shows satisfaction at her choice and then points out that he can roll his tongue as well. Later, Liara tells James she's going to challenge him to a pull\-up contest, something which causes James to give pause, unsure if he should accept the challenge. If Shepard favors biotics, Vega reluctantly accepts the decision. In the next stage of the party, James demonstrates the result of the debate. If Shepard sided with biotics, Liara gives James a demonstration of her powers by biotically lifting him with seemingly no effort. Vega comments on feeling "fuzzy" all over, "among other things." If Shepard chose physical training instead, Vega (plus Jacob and/or Kaidan if they're present) do push\-ups. If Kasumi is also around, she sits on top of Vega while cloaked. Vega naturally finds it difficult to keep up with Jacob, much to his consternation. Kasumi finally reveals herself when Vega is tired out and the marine collapses at that instant. When the party gets lively, Vega may flirt with Ashley if she is present. Shepard can either encourage the exchange or tell them to cool it. If encouraged, Vega continues his playful banter, attempting to woo her with the Spanish phrase *"tú con tantas curvas, y yo sin frenos"* (“you with such curves, and me with no brakes”). Ashley, amused, keeps asking him to repeat it until Vega becomes confused—ultimately resulting in nothing more than lighthearted, harmless flirting. If they don't continue flirting, James instead dances with the other balcony guests. He favors a fist\-pumping moveset akin to aerobic exercise. In the morning after the party, he cooks eggs for the guests, encouraging them all to try his eggs.

Days after the destruction of Bahak, the galaxy is in turmoil over Commander Shepard's alleged actions. While the Citadel Council denounces the Commander and Councilor Udina deflects blame from the Systems Alliance, the Batarian Hegemony calls for retribution for the apparent terrorist acts. On Omega, Alliance soldier James Vega plays cards in a bar as he watches a newscast about the uproar. Without warning, he rips the screen from the wall, offering to pay the krogan bartender for the damages. The batarians Vega was playing cards with become confrontational and accuse him of being a "Shepard Lover". Vega tries to calm them down, but they charge him. He bashes one batarian over the head with the screen, then rushes the leader of another group, both of them crashing through a window. The rest of the batarians surround Vega and attack. The fight is interrupted by the arrival of Admiral Anderson and a contingent of soldiers. Anderson informs Vega that he is being brought in for more training. As they board an aircar, Anderson tells Vega that he must get past "the incident on Fehl" and "be the soldier \[they] expect of \[him]". Vega argues, demanding that Anderson throw him in the brig as they approach the Normandy SR\-2. Anderson then explains that Vega will actually be guarding the brig, and one special prisoner: Commander Shepard.

Biotiball on the Big Screen. 2186, Citadel shore leave, before or after the party Shepard's personal apartment, in front of the vid screen Cortez only sends the invitation if Shepard has helped him reach some closure over his husband's death.

Biotiball on the Big Screen. 2186, Citadel shore leave, before or after the party Shepard's personal apartment, in front of the vid screen Both make their case. Cortez teases that James backs the Maestros because their players are beautiful asari rather than for any skill, and James sheepishly admits he has the hots for them.

Biotiball on the Big Screen. 2186, Citadel shore leave, before or after the party Shepard's personal apartment, in front of the vid screen Cortez writes it up: the Seattle Sorcerers against the Usaru Maestros, Shepard has just acquired an apartment with a sweet vid screen, and neither he nor James thinks that is a coincidence. Shepard provides the couch; they bring the refreshments.

After Shepard's escape from the first run\-in with CAT6, Cortez loiters in the study room of the apartment. He's relieved the Commander got out as none of them expected the attack, so he shares an illuminating lesson learned from the event: "Never have dinner with Joker." If Shepard and Steve are lovers, he admonishes Shepard with another one: "You sneak off to a dinner date with another man, you get shot at." Cortez provides assistance during the infiltration into the Spectre Archives as part of Team Hammerhead, and provides suppressive fire with an M\-8 Avenger alongside the rest of the crew. While Shepard and company fight the Clone to retake the Normandy, Cortez and Joker fly a skycar directly ahead of the Normandy's trajectory, preventing the merc pilot from making the jump to FTL. Cortez utilises the full extent of his piloting skills to evade the Normandy's weapons fire. Once the clone is defeated, Cortez brings a restrained Maya Brooks to Shepard. When Joker compliments his "crazy stunt flying" in the shuttle, Cortez says it was nice to fly something more responsive than the Kodiak; if Cortez and Shepard are romantically involved, he'll instead respond that he was "motivated", followed by a sly wink at the Commander. After taking back the Normandy from the Clone, Cortez will send Shepard an invitation to the Silversun Strip. Steve picks Shepard up at the appointed location with the Kodiak to go on a joyride. Steve reveals during the ride that he has disabled the inertial dampeners and gives Shepard a taste of flight without mass effect fields, something which was commonplace before the advent of mass effect technology. If they are involved in a romance, Shepard can choose to hold hands and then cuddle in the back of the Kodiak while it flies on autopilot. Cortez can also be invited up to Shepard's apartment, along with James Vega, before or after the party. He will send an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. He will wish to watch the biotiball game featuring the Seattle Sorcerers taking on the Usaru Maestros. Both Cortez and Vega will state their cases for each team to win. Shepard will be asked to back a team. Selecting a particular team will result in the supporter of that team winning the bet (though the Sorcerers always win the game). When Shepard questions this, the winner reveals that the bet was only on whether the Commander would be correct in their pick, rather than who would actually win. After the game, both of them thank Shepard and leave the apartment. If Cortez is romanced, James will tell them to enjoy their evening and leave the two of them to cuddle on the couch. Cortez can be invited to the party. In the beginning, he hangs out with James, Ashley/Kaidan and Jack (if they're present). Cortez thanks Shepard for throwing the party and bringing everyone together. If the party setting was chosen to be energetic by Shepard, sometime later, Cortez is at the bar with Joker along with by Garrus, Javik, and Wrex (if they're present). Cortez gets into an argument with Joker regarding their choices of planets most harsh to life. He shows an interest in Prothean fighter craft which he discusses with Javik. At this point, Cortez gets into another argument with Joker regarding the latter's lack of gun training. Cortez insists on taking Joker to the shooting range while Joker insists that he doesn't need to because of EDI. Shepard can either support Joker or Cortez. If Shepard supports Cortez, Joker will agree to go to a gun range to practice, conditional on Cortez beating him in a drinking match. However, Joker's alcoholic concoction (a combination of "horse choker" and mouthwash) leads Cortez to surrender. If Shepard supports Joker, the argument ends. Later, if the party is energetic, Cortez starts dancing with a few friends. He applauds the Commander if they step into dance and comments its nice to see Shepard relaxing once in a while. He is the only person in that group who doesn't tease Shepard about their dancing style.
Steve Cortez drinks mescal late into the nights if he chooses to loosen up, although he relates to James Vega that he'd rather have some tequila.

Once the evacuation of Grissom Academy is completed and if Jack was present, Vega speaks appreciatively of her, saying that she is a tough woman, then adds that she is "hot." Vega also comments on the relationship between Anderson and Kahlee Sanders, saying that they make a nice couple. He speaks of his dad having a surname of "Sanders", clarifying that he and Kahlee are not related. After the krogan female's retrieval from Sur'Kesh, if Wrex was present, Vega admires Wrex for his tough guy attitude and is interested in hearing some of the old krogan's stories. If Mordin was also present, Vega finds his habit of speaking very fast quite funny, saying that "Mordin's mouth moves faster than a frog on a hot rock in the middle of summer." If Padok Wiks is present, Vega says that he finds the salarian to be be very strange, even compared to other salarians. Upon completing the investigation into rachni on Utukku, James shakes his head in amazement at Shepard's ability to find trouble. If Grunt was present, James quips that he is crazier than Shepard, but Shepard is better looking. After rescuing a turian platoon from Tuchanka, Vega compares the deserts there with those back on Earth, saying that the lizards and the worms are bigger on Tuchanka. He also remarks that the Primarch's son is in over his head. Once the Cerberus bomb was defused at the cost of Tarquin Victus' life, Vega sadly states that he would have liked to know Tarquin better. After the mission to cure the genophage, Vega comically asks Shepard if the cure they dispersed could affect them, lest they suddenly start growing scales. He also hopes that they can put aside the diplomacy and go back to fighting the Reapers. James occasionally chats with Cortez while off duty. At one time, he debates with Cortez on the topic: M35 Mako vs M44 Hammerhead. James asserts that the Mako is vastly superior to the Hammerhead, with its powerful cannon and durable armor triumphing over the Hammerhead's inability to take hits. Cortez disagrees, saying the Hammerhead's mobility and maneuverability more than makes up for its low durability. When James says that the Mako doesn't need mobility owing to the presence of a very powerful cannon, Cortez laughs and sarcastically suggests that the M29 Grizzly is more suitable for James. James immediately says that he loves that tank, leading to a snort from Cortez and a remark that only James would like grizzly bears. Yet another time, James congratulates Cortez for "loosening up" a little. When Cortez expresses misgivings over drinking mescal late into the night, James says that it gives one heart which is needed to fight the war. Cortez disagrees, saying it would give him heartburn and moans about not finding decent tequila. James suggests Cortez should be responsible for setting up drinks as a procurement specialist and asks him to set the up. After stopping Udina's coup on the Citadel, James reveals that he knew Udina was a dirty bastard, but never guessed the Councilor was that rotten. After giving his thoughts on Udina to Shepard, he complains about people not seeing that they have to work together if they are going to win the fight against the Reapers, but Shepard tells him that when people are scared they are slow to trust. James agrees but also states he's adopting a 'shoot first, ask questions later' policy when dealing with politicians. Shepard finds that fair enough. Eventually, Vega asks to speak to Shepard privately. After Shepard invites Vega to the Captain's Cabin using the intercom, Vega explains he has been approached with an offer from the Systems Alliance to undergo N7 training. However, Vega is unsure whether or not to accept the offer since N7 training is a lot of work, and Vega humbly wonders why he was even approached, given his past failure, hence the private conversation. He also confesses that during that mission, his team was betrayed by a colonist who was actually a Cerberus spy working with the Collectors. Vega had no choice but to kill the spy and destroy the Collector ship, which left himself, a civilian, and one other squad member as the sole survivors of the mission. Shepard can either encourage Vega to go for it without hesitation or tell him that a decision such like that is one only he can make. James asks the Commander to refrain from mentioning his current situation to anyone. Shepard accepts, and James thanks them. James announces his intent to go back to the hangar, claiming that things are too soft around Shepard's cabin, though Shepard says the bed is much harder than it looks.

- According to Dusty Everman, early designs of Cortez gave him a lighter skin color, which was why many of his scenes are darkly lit, as there was not enough time to adjust them to his final skin tone. Casey Hudson picked the final design of the character. - According to Mark Meer, he recorded many variations for Shepard's reaction to Cortez's death, depending on how much the player interacts with him. However, the game only used the "STEEVE!" recording, which was meant to be only heard if Cortez actually died and Shepard romanced him. - Cortez uses Incinerate during battles in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel mission Citadel Archives: Escape. - Cortez has mission\-related comments in the Normandy shuttle bay after completing the various "N7" Galaxy at War missions when the primary squadmates do not, though James Vega frequently chimes in. ##

James Vega talks to Shepard over comms saying he is coming to assist when the Spectre is being pursued by CAT6 mercenaries. If Urdnot Wrex is not alive, James Vega appears instead and fires a Cobra Missile Launcher at the C\-Sec shuttle carrying CAT6 troops, then supports Shepard and their ally as they fend off more CAT6 forces. James sends Shepard an email sometime after the incident requesting face time in the personal apartment. If Shepard invites him over, James initially starts with giving his opinion on the apartment, steering the conversation to romantic relationships and claiming he stopped fraternizing before he joined the military. Vega expresses interest in the Commander's "personal life", particularly with potential shipmate paramours, and adjusts his inquiries as much. Due to all the flirty banter between a female Shepard and James he says he can't really tell if the Commander is just yanking his chain, and Shepard may reply indicating she's actually interested or confirm she's just keeping him on his toes. If Shepard already has someone else, Vega instead asks if he's getting in the way between Shepard and her current love, and the Commander assures him he's not. If Shepard is in a relationship with either Garrus or Tali, James voices curiosity on the pairing, asking in particular about differences in "anatomy". Too awkward a topic, he just withdraws the question, claiming he doesn't really want to know. Vega also approves of a Shepard/Steve relationship, saying that although he likes to give Esteban a hard time the shuttle pilot is still a great guy who has been through a lot. With Shepard's goading, James finally states his purpose on dropping by: he takes off his shirt to show off his N7 tattoo. Regardless of Shepard's gender or romantic entanglements, James reaffirms his commitment to the mission, and takes his leave claiming Esteban needs his help working on the Normandy's shuttle. As James turns to leave, he discovers the punching bag in the lower bedroom and tells the Commander that they've been holding out on him, proceeding to exercise on the punching bag. Shepard can then interact with the bar between the bedroom and closet, and in doing so, may choose to perform a pull\-up. If so, James comments that his record is 182, and challenges the Commander to beat it. If not, James will either ask about a mulligan or else state that he saw Shepard do nothing. If Shepard accepts James's challenge, James comments on his CO's performance at certain landmarks, i.e. 10, 20, 50, 91 (half his record), 100 and around 110 (where he states most people would be happy with 100\). If the Commander does beat Vega's record, he's so amazed he is at a loss for words and merely asks how Shepard is doing. If Shepard feels they can do another round, James scoffs and defers to their judgement. If Shepard admits to needing help putting on armor next time, James' reaction has a few variations: he's eager to help on a female Shepard who allowed to call her "Lola", he feels the male Shepard earned the nickname "Loco" for the stunt, and if neither of these James deems the stunt itself loco. Regardless of the circumstances, Vega tells Shepard that they still got it, and advises not to let anyone tell them otherwise. Should Shepard fail more than twice to do a significant number of pullups, James will instead marvel at having seen something that Shepard isn't good at. While on shore leave, James also spends his time plying Silversun Strip's many diversions, like combat\-oriented games on Castle Arcade or Armax Arsenal Arena. Shepard may even take him along as a squad member for the latter if the Spectre wishes it. If Shepard is female and in a relationship with Garrus, James turns up in the upper bar of Silver Coast Casino, loitering by the kiosk when two familiar figures start dominating the dance floor. A small crowd gathers watching Shepard and Vakarian do the tango, James among them, and he expresses sly amusement when Shepard swings by in front of him. Cortez sends an e\-mail asking for an invitation, if Shepard has helped him reach a sense of closure on his husband's death. Both Cortez and Vega state their cases for each team to win. Vega backs the Maestros and is teased by Cortez for it, who cites Vega's support of the Maestros is mostly due to their players being beautiful asari, than their actual skill. Vega sheepishly admits he has got the "hots" for the Maestro players. Shepard is asked to back a team.

evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-2 (Part 4) — The Alliance Refit
evidence.text: Contains the armory, cargo hold, and two Kodiak shuttles. James Vega and Lieutenant Steve Cortez spend their time here. A procurement terminal sells equipment from various retailers at a slight premium over Citadel prices; a weapon modification bench, an armor locker, and a small gym are also here.

The Party at Shepard's Apartment. 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Lieutenant Steve Cortez was an Alliance pilot aboard the Normandy SR-2 in 2186, flying the UT-47A Kodiak that carried Commander Shepard and squad to missions, and a potential romance option for a male Shepard. An only child who lost both parents years earlier, Cortez had a husband, Robert, who was killed when the Collectors abducted the colony of Ferris Fields in 2185; Robert phoned Steve during the attack to tell him to escape and let him go. Steve kept a recording of the call and grieved heavily. He had served in the Alliance since around 2176, first in the First Fleet aboard the SSV Hawking flying F-61 Tridents, and five months before the Reaper invasion joined the Normandy SR-2 retrofit team, moving the armory to the shuttle bay.

Aboard the Normandy, Cortez maintained the armory alongside Lt. James Vega, an old friend from Fehl Prime, and preferred to keep busy to avoid thinking about Robert. Shepard could persuade him to take shore leave on the Citadel; he later visited the refugees' Memorial Wall to say goodbye to Robert and began to move on, reconnecting with old pilot friends and forwarding their information to Admiral Hackett to give the Alliance more pilots. A meeting at Purgatory could begin a relationship with a male Shepard or reinforce their friendship.

During the final assault on Earth, Cortez's shuttle was shot down by a Harvester after dropping off the squad. If he had visited the Memorial Wall he survived the crash and could be contacted by hologram; otherwise he died and Vega confirmed it, and his name appeared on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez." In the Leviathan DLC he crash-landed the shuttle and devised the plan for Shepard to reach Leviathan using a Triton mech. In the Citadel DLC he provided suppressive fire during the Spectre Archives infiltration, flew a skycar with Joker to block the hijacked Normandy from jumping to FTL, delivered a restrained Maya Brooks, and could take Shepard on a joyride in the Kodiak with the inertial dampeners disabled. If the Crucible was activated and the Reapers were controlled or Synthesis was chosen, Cortez placed Shepard's name on the memorial wall.

Besides being a Kodiak pilot aboard the Normandy SR\-2, Steve is also responsible for maintaining the Normandy's armory, a duty he shares with Lt. James Vega. Cortez and Vega are friends, having served together before on Fehl Prime. In between missions, they engage in off duty conversations. Cortez prefers to have as little time off from his duties as possible, since any time spent not working gives him too much time to think about Robert. Shepard has the option of convincing Cortez to take time off to leave the ship and succeeds. At first, Steve just loiters near the Normandy's docking bay on the Citadel, but he finds Shepard's suggestion a good idea since the vista of so many ships in flight brings him comfort and gets him thinking. He later visits the Memorial Wall for victims of Collector and Reaper attacks at the refugee docks, where Shepard can once more offer words of support. The downtime helps him to move on, and he meets up with some old pilot friends and forwards their information to Admiral Hackett, giving the Alliance some much needed pilots. A further encounter at Purgatory allows a male Shepard to begin a relationship with him, or reinforces their friendship otherwise. During the final assault on Earth, after dropping off Shepard's squad, Cortez's shuttle is shot down by a Harvester. If he has been persuaded to visit the Memorial Wall, he survives the crash and can be contacted via hologram later. Steve is later present in front of the Normandy's memorial wall with the rest of Shepard's surviving crew if the Crucible was activated, paying his respects to the dead. If Steve was never interacted with much, he dies when his shuttle gets shot during the final assault on Earth. He cannot be contacted and James confirms Cortez's death. Much later, if Shepard uses the Crucible, Steve's name is listed on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez".

This page catalogs in-universe forms of recreation across the Milky Way and Andromeda: films, plays, books, magazines, musical acts, sports, and games. Notable theatrical works included Francis Kitt's award-winning all-elcor production of Hamlet, which ran over 14 hours and used elcor body language and pheromones, and his planned Macbeth with a krogan lead and a live pyjak; the elcor doctor Yorrik authored an unproduced 16-hour all-elcor Macbeth but died before reaching Andromeda. Starless (2173) was a gothic horror masterpiece whose vacuum-preserved sets on airless Faringor became a tourist draw.

The Blasto franchise followed the galaxy's first hanar Spectre through many films, including Blasto: the Jellyfish Stings, Blasto Saves Christmas, Blasto 6: Partners in Crime, and Blasto 7: Blasto Goes to War! (co-starring Shepard and Javik). Blasto lines quoted include: "This one doesn't have time for your solid waste excretions." / "This one has forgotten whether its heatsink is over capacity. It wonders whether the criminal scum considers itself fortunate?" / "Enkindle THIS."

Citadel, directed by Risa Uvarsen, dramatized Shepard's role in the Eden Prime War, with a scene varying by whether Shepard saved the Council. Fleet and Flotilla was an award-winning vid praised for its positive turian-quarian romance; Shepard and Tali could watch it during Citadel shore leave. Its quoted lines: Bellicus, "But Shalei. We can never be together. I have my duty, and you, have your people." / Shalei, "Not tonight. Tonight, I'm as free as the dust in the solar wind." / Shalei, "I want you to see behind this mask. I want you to see who I truly am." / Bellicus, "I already have." Last of the Legion was a turian war film watched aboard the Tempest, quoted: Jorax Halabrian, "I never left the Legion. It left me. But I know my duty." Nekyia Corridor was a record-breaking human simstim that outgrossed the asari classic Confederates.

Dozens of other films are listed via Cerberus Daily News box-office reports, including Blue Steel, Vaenia, and the "Taetrus effect" comedies. Games covered include Chess (popular with elcor; General Oleg Petrovsky's holographic board passes to Shepard if Omega is liberated), Kepesh-Yakshi, Galaxy of Fantasy, Quasar, Skillian Five poker, and Three-Card-Monte. Publications include Fornax ("the galaxy's finest xenophilia"), Ascension and Revelation by Drew Karpyshyn, and Justicar Heroes. Sports include biotiball, clawball, kailat ring-ball, the krogan sport kowla, and Armax Arsenal Arena combat simulators.

April was a colonist on Fehl Prime in 2185 and the daughter of Christine. She was a lively little girl who idolized the Systems Alliance Marines and worshipped Lieutenant James Vega in particular, their relationship almost like that of brother and sister. She sometimes pretended to be a marine by putting on James's combat helmet.

During the installation of the colony's defense cannon, April came to meet Vega with her mother, snapped him a military salute, and pretended to be a professional. Vega gave her a badge to wear. She teased Vega about looking at Treeya differently from others; Vega deflected by hoisting her onto his shoulders and telling her to act as a lookout for bad guys, which she happily did, imagining herself an Alliance private. When she asked about the large gun the Alliance had installed, Vega promised her he would use it to keep the colony safe.

When the Collectors attacked the colony, April and Christine were paralyzed by the Seeker Swarms, and Delta Squad was forced to watch as the Collectors carried them away to their ship. Later, after Delta Squad infiltrated the Collector ship and released the antidote from the processing plant, April reawakened along with the other colonists. She never gave up hope in Vega, and contacted him over the comm using Toni's omni-tool, telling him to come and save them and that she would always believe in him. evidence.text:
The M35 Mako Infantry Fighting Vehicle was designed for Systems Alliance frigates to provide the rapid deployment its predecessor, the M29 Grizzly, could not. Small enough to ride in a cargo bay and deploy on virtually any world despite a cramped interior, it mounted a turreted 155mm mass accelerator cannon and a coaxial machine gun. It was environmentally sealed, powered by a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, and armored to survive high drops, extreme heat and cold, and rough terrain. Independently reversible wheels let it turn like a tank, and micro-thrusters plus a small element zero core allowed it to adjust mass for traction and be safely air-dropped without the usual 100m of open terrain, limiting a frigate's exposure to anti-aircraft fire. Laser detection arrays and ground-penetrating radar warned the crew of guided ordnance and mines. Support vehicles on the Mako chassis included a recon drone controller, a mobile air defense platform, and the M38 "Moby" military ambulance; shipboard Marines used only the armed base model. It carried eight: two in front and six in the hold.

In Mass Effect, the SSV Normandy carried a Mako that Shepard used to explore most landing sites. On Ilos, Shepard's squad drove it through the Conduit, crossing thousands of lightyears directly to the Citadel Presidium, where it smashed two geth troopers before overturning; badly damaged, it was abandoned. In Mass Effect: Paragon Lost, a merchant named Messner lent a used Mako to James Vega's Delta Squad and archaeologist Treeya Nuwani on Fehl Prime, with Mason and later Milque on its gun; the Collector attack rendered it irrelevant or destroyed. In Mass Effect 2 the Normandy's Mako was repaired or replaced; after the Collector Cruiser destroyed the ship, the Mako was found nearly intact in the ice of Alchera, and the UT-47 Kodiak shuttle became Shepard's primary transport aboard the Normandy SR-2. In Mass Effect 3, Makos formed the bulk of Hammer Team's mobile armor during the final battle for Earth, most destroyed trying to outrun Harbinger near the London Conduit. Named after the mako shark, the vehicle drew design cues from Russian BTR APCs, the Mowag Piranha, and the Big Trak toy. Cut content notes it was called the "rover" internally and spawned designs reused for the skycar, Grizzly, Tomkah, and M-44 Hammerhead.
