evidence.text:
Priority: Earth was the final mission of Mass Effect 3 and the conclusion of Commander Shepard's trilogy. It was acquired after Priority: Cerberus Headquarters; from that point Sol was the only reachable system, and merely traveling there triggered the mission with no way to back out. Allied fleets assaulted the Reapers above Earth while Hammer, the ground force, tried to land troops near the Citadel transport beam.

The mission had two main stages. First, Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" so Hammer could land; the team fought through streets and a ruined house full of Cannibals, Marauders, and Brutes to a crashed assault team, recovered two M-920 Cain shots to destroy the cannon, held off a Banshee (named "Morinth" if that character survived Mass Effect 2) and endless Cannibals, and were extracted, reuniting with Anderson and meeting Major Coats. At the Forward Operating Base, Shepard held final conversations with surviving squadmates, allies, and leaders (Victus, Wrex or Wreav, Kirrahe, and others depending on prior choices) before Anderson gave the battle plan: a frontal armored assault on the conduit past a Reaper Destroyer.

The second stage advanced through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles were coordinated with EDI on the Normandy to destroy the Destroyer while the team fought Brutes, Banshees, and a Harvester and dodged the Reaper's beam. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final push, but Harbinger descended on the conduit and annihilated the ground forces. In the Extended Cut, squadmates survived or died based on Effective Military Strength (below 4200 EMS in Legendary Edition they died). A wounded, solitary Shepard fought through Husks and a Marauder with an infinite-clip pistol to reach the beam.

On the reconfigured Citadel, Shepard reunited by comm with Anderson and found him held hostage by a transformed Illusive Man, who could now control both of them. The confrontation's outcome hinged on the final choice, with full Paragon/Renegade options requiring Paragon/Renegade choices at every prior meeting with the Illusive Man. Paragon made him realize he was indoctrinated and shoot himself; Renegade interrupts let Shepard kill him. Shepard then opened the Citadel arms to let the Crucible dock. The Catalyst appeared and offered Destruction, Control, or Synthesis (Refusal was also possible), with availability and galactic damage set by EMS. Every activated ending crippled the Normandy, and its crew's survival, the epilogue scenes, and the placing of Shepard's name plaque above Anderson's on the memorial wall all depended on EMS and prior choices. After the credits a Stargazer told a child tales of "the Shepard."

evidence.text:
Armistan Banes was a researcher hired by the Systems Alliance who disappeared under mysterious circumstances. In Mass Effect, his name arose when a krogan blackmailer, attempting to extort medical supplies from Dr. Chloe Michel on the Citadel, claimed to be acting on Banes' behalf. Dr. Michel told Commander Shepard that she and Banes had worked together years earlier but had lost contact, and that as far as she knew Banes had been contracted by the Alliance military for research in the Attican Traverse. A squad member suggested Shepard ask Captain Anderson.

When asked, Anderson was surprised, questioned where Shepard had heard the name, then decided he did not want to know. He revealed that Banes had been dead for some time, a fact not publicly known, and that Banes' corpse had been found on a derelict ship in the Sparta system. Anderson could say no more and directed Shepard to Rear Admiral Kahoku, whose crew had recovered the body. Speaking with Kahoku, Shepard learned that the marines who found the corpse had themselves gone missing. Because of the "classified project" Anderson mentioned and the fate of Kahoku's marines, Banes may have been involved in a Cerberus-sponsored project. To pursue the full chain of leads, the assignment Citadel: Doctor Michel had to be completed before UNC: Missing Marines, since Kahoku left the Citadel afterward.

In Mass Effect 3, if Dr. Michel was invited aboard the Normandy SR-2 instead of Dr. Chakwas, and Shepard visited the crew quarters directly after the Sur'Kesh mission with Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks temporarily aboard, Dr. Michel and Engineer Adams could be overheard talking. Dr. Michel clarified that she had once worked with Armistan Banes, that she had believed he was with the Alliance, but that he had turned out to be a Cerberus agent.

evidence.text:
The N7 Crusader was a shotgun appearing in Mass Effect 3 and Mass Effect: Andromeda. In-universe, bruised and bloody Alliance marines on Torfan credited their survival against waves of batarian mercenaries to the Crusader's precision and stopping power. Patterned on riot shotguns, it had a moderate rate of fire that rewarded careful aiming and was primarily issued to highly trained soldiers.

Unlike a normal shotgun, the Crusader fired a single high-powered slug rather than a spread of pellets, firing four semi-automatic shots before reloading. It had innate 50 cm shot penetration, punching through thin obstacles, Guardian shields and armor plating with no damage penalty. It was very accurate, with accuracy improving when aimed down sights, and its damage per shot exceeded the M-99 Saber and rivaled sniper rifles like the M-92 Mantis, though it was one of the heaviest weapons in the game with heavy vertical recoil and a 0.1-second delay between trigger pull and firing. Its single-projectile design made it strong against armor but more vulnerable to shield gates, mitigated by Disruptor Ammo.

In Mass Effect 3 single-player it came with the N7 Collector's Edition Pack, delivered via an email from Lieutenant D. Eugene of the Alliance Engineering Corps, who had led the Normandy's Alliance retrofit; in Legendary Edition it cost 125,000 credits at Spectre Requisitions. In multiplayer it was ultra-rare. In Mass Effect: Andromeda the Initiative's N7 Crusaders were heavily modified versions supplied by a sympathetic Systems Alliance agent. The name references the medieval Crusades.

The UNAS was one of many Earth nations invaded by the Reapers in 2186 CE. Commander Shepard was present in the city of Vancouver as the first Reaper forces landed there, and escaped on the Normandy SR\-2. Simultaneously, reporter Emily Wong witnessed the invasion at Los Angeles and transmitted her experience via a Quantum Entanglement Communicator, one of the few communication systems that continued to function after the Reapers destroyed the comm buoy networks, GPS and communications satellites, and undersea fiber\-optic cables. The Reapers bombarded military bases, nuclear missile silos, industrial centers, and completely annihilated cities with populations in the low millions, including Fort Worth. Due to the communications blackout, no other details about the state of the UNAS during the Reaper occupation are known.

Prologue: Earth is the opening mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically at the start of the game. It serves as the game's tutorial. After character customization and a series of cutscenes with morality-point dialogue, Shepard enters a training stage in war-torn Vancouver during the Reaper invasion. Anderson gives Shepard an M-3 Predator pistol, and the two move across rooftops while Oculi destroy Alliance fighters overhead. Shepard encounters husks climbing a wall and a child fleeing toward a building; Anderson eventually runs out of ammo and climbs down a ladder. Shepard fights husks in melee before a Reaper fires its laser at an adjacent building.

Moving through the ruins, Shepard opens a med kit, briefly encounters the boy again, and then witnesses an Alliance vessel destroyed by a Reaper while Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko comments over the radio. Shepard reaches two Alliance soldiers and fights the first engagement against Cannibals, which here do not use grenades. Anderson can now deal damage and be assigned squad points. After crossing a bridge, salvaging a second med kit, and picking up an M-8 Avenger, Shepard activates a radio and fights further Cannibal waves until the Normandy SR-2 arrives and clears the remaining enemies.

Shepard says goodbye to Anderson, who stays on Earth. The boy is killed when the Kodiak evacuating him is shot down by a Destroyer. The Normandy leaves Vancouver, passing burning human fleets. Aboard ship, James Vega is incredulous that Shepard intends to follow Anderson's orders and leave Earth to seek the Citadel Council's aid; the exchange allows Paragon or Renegade interrupts. Admiral Hackett then contacts Shepard and assigns the next mission, Priority: Mars.

Enemies are Cannibals and Husks. Rewards include three units of medi-gel, the M-3 Predator, and the M-8 Avenger. Trivia notes Vancouver was chosen because BioWare is a Canadian company; the ship shown destroyed is actually an Alliance cruiser rather than the dreadnought Ashley or Kaidan describe, a discrepancy noted in SolComms reports by Emily Wong; and fleeing civilians visible in the distance are 2D sprites resembling Jack.

A temperate world that has hit the "sweet spot" for carbon\-based life, **Horizon** has a nitrogen\-oxygen atmosphere maintained by abundant plants and bacteria. Its soil is particularly compatible with Earth vegetation, and so a thriving human community has sprung up. Horizon's population is in flux. A Collector attack in 2185 inflicted significant casualties, but refugees have been streaming to the planet since the Reaper invasion began. Since many land illegally, there is no way to accurately track population. Although many colonists resent the newcomers, others have embraced Horizon's new role. Advertisements for "Sanctuary," its main refugee center, can be seen galaxy\-wide.

Six months have passed since the destruction of Bahak and Commander Shepard's voluntary return to the Alliance. The Commander has been relieved of command and detained in a Systems Alliance facility in the city of Vancouver on Earth. Without warning, Alliance deep space outposts beyond Sol begin to go dark. Admiral Steven Hackett, the head of the Alliance military, begins to prepare for an imminent invasion. Admiral David Anderson arrives in Vancouver and escorts Commander Shepard with Lieutenant James Vega to a meeting with an Alliance defense committee. Shepard confirms their worst fears: the Reapers have returned to the galaxy and are on their way to Earth. At that moment, contact is lost with Luna Base and news reports begin to surface of an unknown alien force landing in Earth's cities. The Reapers have already arrived. A Reaper capital ship then descends through the clouds over Vancouver and blasts the Alliance building, killing the defense committee and Alliance staff. Shepard and Anderson survive and contact Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko (whichever survived Virmire), telling them to get to the Normandy. As Shepard and Anderson make their way from building to building to get to the spaceport, Anderson tells Shepard that they have to get to the Citadel and seek help from the Council. They reach a comm set near a crashed gunship and hail the Normandy to evacuate. After holding off an attack from Cannibals, the Normandy bombs the area clear of attackers. As Shepard boards the ship, Anderson informs the Commander that he will stay behind to lead the resistance, and hands over Shepard's dog tags. Shepard protests, but Anderson charges Shepard with getting as much help as possible to save Earth and stop the Reapers. As the Normandy lifts off, Shepard witnesses a child running to an Alliance evacuation area and boarding a shuttle. As the shuttles lift off, a Reaper destroyer emerges from behind a cluster of buildings and targets the shuttles, killing those who were aboard including the child. Distraught, Shepard steps away from the open shuttle bay doors of the Normandy, and the ship escapes Earth as more Reapers and the wreckage of Alliance ships rain down upon the planet.
Husks return en masse during the Reaper invasion of 2186 and make up the bulk of the Reapers' ground forces. They are first encountered during the invasion of Earth.

*Main article: Harbinger* Class Capital Ship Affiliation Reaper Believed to be the oldest and largest Reaper. Instigated the Collector attacks on human colonies in 2185, and participated in the Reaper invasion of Earth in 2186\. Source Mass Effect 2

During the initial Reaper invasion of Earth, FCC News reporter Emily Wong managed to secure a Quantum Entanglement Communicator (QEC) from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA). With it she was able to live\-cast the opening hours of the Reaper invasion via the Alliance News Network despite the Earth communication buoys having been disabled by the Reapers. The information capable of being transmitted by the QEC was limited to short burst messages, some of which were garbled by interference. Each message was appended with the tag \#solcomms, as it was assumed to be the only communication with the Sol system during the invasion. **ANN** (@AllianceNewsNet) comm channel: The reporter Emily Wong is transmitting her short messages via the ANN comm channel.

The Seventh Fleet was stationed near Eden Prime at the time of the Reaper invasion in 2186\. Instead of being directly engaged in battle, the Reapers bypassed the Seventh Fleet entirely on their way to Earth.

Multiplayer map page. Firebase Vancouver is a Mass Effect 3 multiplayer map included in the Mass Effect 3: Earth DLC, set on rooftops in Vancouver. Its areas are the Helipad (starting location and a possible extraction zone), Lower Rooftops, Upper Rooftops (lower level a possible extraction zone), Offices (a medical wing), Ventilation Deck, and Ventilation Housing. Like Firebase Dagger, it has two possible extraction locations, close together. The Ventilation Deck is difficult to navigate for classes that cannot climb cover, and area-of-effect powers can singlehandedly halt massed infantry at chokepoints such as the ladder by the Offices.

Docks: Holding Area was a location on the Citadel Presidium, directly below Normandy Dock: Bay D24. It had formerly been reserved for Alliance embassy deliveries, but during the Reaper invasion Councilor Udina issued a unanimously approved Council motion to repurpose the docks into emergency civilian housing, funded by all the major races. Adjacent sections E24, E26, and E28 were converted into a refugee camp, and the refugee population grew over time.

Points of interest included a security checkpoint where a refugee pleaded with a dock officer to admit his family (Shepard could side with either, affecting War Assets), and where Solik Vass appeared after the attack on the Citadel. Bay E24 held Avina and, during the medi-gel sabotage investigation, Conrad Verner. Bay E28 was where James Vega often played poker. Cargo Hold A held Garrus Vakarian before the Citadel attack, a Shepard VI store model, and Darner Vosque or Sayn during the recruitment of the Blue Suns and Eclipse for Aria. Cargo Hold B held Kelly Chambers (if she survived the Collectors and was invited to dinner), a doctor working on medi-gel sabotage, and the refugee leader Tactus. Cargo Hold C held the Batarian State Arms terminal, a batarian preacher, Zaeed Massani (after the volus ambassador mission), and the injured batarian terrorist Ghorek. The Memorial Wall was where Steve Cortez mourned his late husband and Ashley Williams comforted her sister.

Missions tied to the area included Aria: Blue Suns, Aria: Eclipse, Citadel: Batarian Codes, Citadel: Hanar Diplomat, Citadel: Inspirational Stories, Citadel: Medical Supplies, Citadel: Medi-Gel Sabotage, Citadel: Wounded Batarian, Hades Nexus: Prothean Sphere, and Kite's Nest: Pillars of Strength.

The United North American States (UNAS) was a coalition on Earth at the time of the Mass Effect trilogy, formed in the late 21st century when Canada, Mexico, and the United States of America merged. The union, established around 2096 CE, was strongly opposed by secessionist factions including the extremist group Freedoms First. On the morning of November 1, 2096, the New York chapter of Freedoms First attacked Liberty Island and destroyed the Statue of Liberty, and the resulting outrage triggered the Second American Civil War between secessionists and UNAS forces.

In 2149 CE, following the discovery of a cache of Prothean technology on Mars, the UNAS and seventeen other nations ratified the Systems Alliance charter, and the UNAS contributed military assets to the new Alliance military. When the garden world Watson was discovered in 2165 CE, the UNAS, the Chinese People's Federation, and the European Union all claimed it; the Alliance brokered the Reykjavik Compromise allowing each to settle its own colonies there.

In 2176 CE, UNAS President Enrique Aguilar was assassinated during a photo opportunity with Chinese People's Federation premier Ying Xiong. The killer, patent clerk and dissident Michael Moser Lang of Virginia, concealed a Kassa Fabrication M-12 Locust submachine gun inside a shoulder-mounted video camera. His first burst broke through the stage's kinetic barriers; Xiong tried to shield Aguilar, but Lang's next shots passed through Xiong and killed both men. During his term, President Christopher Huerta suffered a stroke that left him legally dead for 90 minutes before his brain functions were transferred to a computer. In 2185 CE, Speaker of the House Lisa Ford brought the case Ford v. Huerta, arguing his time in office afterward was illegitimate and that she should have been Vice President; the Systems Alliance heard the case and ruled 5-4 that Huerta's continued term was legitimate, prompting protests in several UNAS cities.

The UNAS was one of many Earth nations invaded by the Reapers in 2186 CE. Commander Shepard was in Vancouver as the first Reaper forces landed and escaped aboard the Normandy SR-2, while reporter Emily Wong witnessed the invasion at Los Angeles and transmitted her account via a Quantum Entanglement Communicator. The Reapers bombarded military bases, missile silos, and industrial centers and annihilated cities of low millions, including Fort Worth; the communications blackout meant little else was known about the UNAS during the occupation. Mentioned cities included New York City, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Toronto, Ottawa, Washington D.C., and the Texan Megapolis of Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, and San Antonio.

codex.text: - April was a young colonist on Fehl Prime in 2185, daughter of Christine, who idolized Lieutenant James Vega; she was abducted by the Collectors and died with the other colonists when the Collector ship crashed before evacuation (source: April).

- Archuk was the ruthless krogan leader of a Blood Pack squad that besieged the human colony of Fehl Prime in 2183, breaking its kinetic barriers with a bomb; he defeated James Vega in a duel but was killed by Milque's sniper rifle (source: Archuk).

- Christine: determined human colonist on Fehl Prime and mother of April, from Mass Effect: Paragon Lost; she rallied the colonists during the 2183 Blood Pack siege, buying time for Alliance marines. In 2185 she and April were abducted by the Collectors; revived aboard the Collector ship, they died with all the other colonists when James Vega's choice led to the ship crashing. (source: Christine)

- Messner was a Cerberus operative posing as a traveling trader who deliberately lured the Collectors to Fehl Prime in 2185 to study them, sacrificing the colony; he killed the krogan pilot Brood, forced Treeya to access a Prothean archive aboard the Collector ship, and was killed by James Vega after being left to Collector fire. (source: Messner)

- Milque was a cynical human sniper of the Alliance's Delta Squad on Fehl Prime, armed with an M-92 Mantis; he fought the Blood Pack and later the Collectors alongside James Vega, as depicted in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost.

- Nicky was the shy technical specialist of Delta Squad on Fehl Prime in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost, who deployed a Combat Drone against the Blood Pack and was mortally wounded by a Praetorian's leg while shoving James Vega clear. (source: Nicky)

- On Fehl Prime in 2183 Toni's Kodiak was shot down by Blood Pack missile launchers; he dislocated his leg, fell unconscious, and command passed to James Vega, who led the counterattack (source: Toni).

- Treeya Nuwani was a pacifist asari anthropologist and archaeologist on Fehl Prime, a student of Liara T'Soni, oblivious to James Vega's romantic interest, in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost (source: Treeya Nuwani).

- Among Delta Squad on Fehl Prime, sniper Milque ran a long-running gag of demanding "free drinks" from Lieutenant James Vega as payment for covering him in combat, escalating his price to "free drinks for life" after saving Vega from a krogan Battlemaster; he also mocked squadmate Nicky as a "kiss-ass" for repeatedly calling Vega "sir" against orders, and kept needling Vega over his stumbling attempts to court the asari Treeya. (source: Milque)
- James Vega and Steve Cortez were friends, having served together on Fehl Prime before their assignment to the Normandy. (source: Steve Cortez)

- On Fehl Prime, colonist child April idolized Lieutenant James Vega almost like an older brother, saluting him, wearing his combat helmet, and teasing him about looking at Treeya differently from other people; Vega deflected by hoisting her onto his shoulders and having her "stand lookout." (source: April)
